concept: Two springs in series share the same pull, so together they are softer than either one.
goal: Discover that the total stretch is the weight divided by the combined stiffness, and that Mars pulls less than Earth.
phenomenon: Two springs hang one below the other from a bar. A mass hangs from the lower spring. Both springs stretch as the mass settles, and each stretches in proportion to its own softness.

interactions.target: the hanger under the lower spring
interactions.response: the springs stretch as the mass settles

interactions.target: along the weak to strong gravity scale
interactions.response: the springs shorten or lengthen as gravity changes

interactions.target: along the stiffness scale beside the spring
interactions.response: the upper spring's coils tighten or loosen

interactions.target: along the stiffness scale beside the spring
interactions.response: the lower spring's coils tighten or loosen

scene.apparatus: two springs hanging from a bar with a mass hanger and a mass tray
fills: a stiffness scale for each spring
scene.wideScreen: The bench is centred; the ruler and the stiffness scales stand to its left and right so no side is empty.

motion: The springs stretch smoothly as the mass settles and ease back when it is lifted. Under reduced motion they jump to the final length.

expectedBehaviour.text: the total stretch rises as the mass rises
the total extension falls as spring 1 gets stiffer
the total stretch stays between 0 and 300 cm

predict.question: On Mars, will the same mass stretch the two springs more or less than on Earth?
predict.check: Drop 200 g on the hanger, then drag the gravity marker to a weaker value.

steps: Drop 200 g from the tray onto the hanger and read the extension on Earth.
Drag the gravity marker to a weaker planet and read the stretch again.
Drag the end ring of spring 2 along its scale to make it stiffer and watch the total stretch fall.
